Sacha: Sacha would make a great politician because he is one of the least irascible people in the Kingdom. Time - Sacha seems to have plenty of it. No one really knows why, although it might be because people are never sure they're meeting a man, and so it take a few seconds to get their head around the fact. By the time they've come to terms with the situation, Sacha has summed them up completely, which has the side effect of producing a calm and surprising environment for everybody. The upshot of all this is that Sacha is a skilled and unassuming leader who enjoys change and a challenge. But yes, when or if he wants to party, you can expect not to be going home before dawn.
Sachen: “Ah, sleeps for pussies!” he barks at 4 in the morning to a dwindling crowd in the lounge room. “Come on! Fuckin’ wake up! I’ve just cracked the last keg!”
Sackie: He balks, he turns, he jumps, occasionally without even looking. But, as a balanced thespian who indulges in the beauty of the small things, his actions always aim to highlight such moments to the world around him. Sackie is an underrated performer.
Saleem: I wonder if he has Lebanese parents? Anyway, like a male Louie before him, Saleem is cool and suave and ever-so-good with the ladies. He rarely works with his hands and he doesn't spend hours and days pondering his own mental processes.
Sam: The name of the human being inside Humphrey B. Bear or Big Bird, if you know either of them. In essence, Sam is funny and friendly, and he can act. Better than that, actually, he doesn’t have a nasty bone in his body.
Samba:
Responsibilities: Capital Zero.
Capacity for hard work and long periods of intense concentration: Capital Zero.
But by god, women adore him and he can dance like no one’s business. 
And Samba is lucky so don’t write him off just coz’ he’s late.
Sammey: Yep, well, whaddaya do? The word falls out of your mouth as easy as pouring a glass of warm milk down a dairy farming hill, and leaves you smiling. What does this mean? Well, Sammey has barely a nasty bone in his body, and the girls he's managed to piss off only got angry because he forgot the instructions he was given. What do you do? There's only so much a country boy can handle at once.
Sammy: Sammy is a textbook knockabout lad who cruises along, quite nicely. As a perpetual optimist people are always happy to see him, and he’s never deliberately hurt anyone who didn’t deserve it.
Samson:
These days you'll often hear people sprout on about how everyone's opinion is none of their business. It's a true statement, give or take, but few people are beholden to this ethos, naturally. Samson is one of these cats. It's not that he's arrogant, and he's definitely not conceited, it's just that Samson was plonked here on Earth by the gods, or whoever tends these matters, to show others how to give unconditional love at all times.
In many ways he's like the Pied Piper. Indeed, he might just be the Pied Piper of Love. Thank you Samson.
Samuel: If Samuel never gets called Sam or Sammy by his friends, then he attended a renowned private boys’ school, dated the girls from the correct private girls’ school and was given a brand new Audi for is 18th birthday. I’ve just asked the boys in the commentary box for any more info and they’re not even listening. Sorry.
Sander: No, he’s probably not originally Australian, American or English but how many of us really are? His Northern European eccentricities make him honest in dealings, easy in company and he is skilled at sliding his way out of a maze.
Sandy: As a retired industrialist who used to deal in rivers of gold, Sandy spends every Friday night in an expensive private mens’ club sucking on his sherry and his cigars, divvying out insider’s-advice to some of the doting young guns who hang on his every word.
Sanjay: Sanjay has all the moves and he knows most of the answers, and if he doesn’t know them he’ll perform a short skit in order to jolt his memory, or the memory of others. Alternately, he’ll perform a skit in order to entertain all of those people aforementioned, just for the hell of it. Has anyone thought of trying to clone him?
Santiago: His cheeky grin hides the fact that he deals with heated situations very well. Like a few other likely lads out there, his moves on the dance floor force one to consider if perhaps he has a living mouse down his underpants, and we're all better off for his exuberance. Peaceful in love and life, Santiago gravitates people towards him and he's not as lazy as you think.
Santino: The extravagant flamingo whose manners and joie de vivre ingratiate him to most people. He does have expensive taste, which is fine, so long as he’s playing with his own money. Know what I mean chief?
Santo: Light-hearted. He instigates the good times and, often, he is actually quite devious. (Note: In a past life his name was Maria.)
Sascha: Surprisingly composed, Sascha holds it all back until it's almost too late. Just when you think he's missed, or screwed up, or waited too long, BANG!, he makes his move. Sascha was not built to live in any kind of office, especially that of an accounting firm. That'd kill him.
Sasha: Sasha will literally froth at the mouth at the prospect of going dancing.
Saul: The tiny marsupial mouse who scurries about in the quiet of the night, going about his business quite happily and very efficiently. No one can tell you what colour his eyes are.
Saverio: Saverio is actually quite humble, although he's rather disappointed by the expectations that people place on him. He's just a normal guy, remember.
Sawyer:
The upbeat man-about-town. Like Deano way before him, he doesn't let a bad situation or an ill-wind prevent him from standing up and saying, "Well, enough of this. I'm off!"

In life he is enjoyed by his colleagues and peers as an eternal optimist, and when he's miserable, which is both rare and funny, actually, you're liable to never know about it.
Saxby: Yeah, Saxby went to New Orleans once. The day after he got there a hurricane tore the city to shreds and he came home with an STD after getting drunk and sleeping with a giant, black prostitute in the back of a van. We think she was a woman.
Saxon:
Well, you can't say he isn't dramatic. Did you know Saxon is the only creature in the entire Kingdom who likes to play the trombone while making love? 

(Just kidding - we WISH he was that inventive in bed.)
Scamp: Predictably, here we have a scamp by name and a scamp by nature. Just imagine for a moment, if you will, that every male in the Middle East sported some kind of analogous (Arabic-sounding) name? A word that bounced and sang and pranced as you said it? I tell you what would happen: Page one line one, violence and hatred would immediately cease. The entire population would suddenly appreciate women and gays, they'd celebrate spiritual and cultural differences, they'd rejoice in spontaneous outbursts of play acting and song, and people would actively share everything with those who were less fortunate. And, fuck me, then we'd have peace on Earth. So, yes, Scamp is not supposed to be serious or overly responsible, and for this we are eternally grateful.
Scooner: The perennial shit-giver who takes nothing seriously.
Scot: If he's going to gamble he won't be doing it out the front with all the drunken cattle from the country, sitting proudly in front of their pile of $2 chips. No sir. He'll be out the back in an exclusive room where the ante ain't for the faint hearted. No one knows what he's thinking and that's just the way he likes it...
Scott: Sure, he picks his nose in public but Scott is young at heart, enthusiastic in life and more ambitious than most.
Scotty: A physically active individual, people meet Scotty for the first time and feel like they know him, and this empathy gives him a huge scope for success. His great skill, however, is to keep a cool head when others begin to panic and if you were on an Irene-affected flight, you’d want Scotty sitting next to you so you could swap jokes until you bought-it.
Scud:
The nickname given to a man who has never left home, and who has therefore failed to launch. 

Note from Management: Careful son, if you don’t sort out your shit it just might stick. Good luck.
Sean: Sean masturbates a tremendous amount, some-times in public, occasionally in car parks.
Seany: It’s a long story, but the short version is that Seany isn’t into long, involved lectures, so university is probably out. What he is great at is making things up on the fly. Don’t give him too many plans right now, give them to him when he asks for them, and whether you think that’s too late or not. He’s just better thinking and planning on his feet.
Sebastian: We would expect Sebastian to be a deep thinker and he nearly gets there. What he is, though, is a complicated and good soul. (Note: If he has blonde hair he is not from Earth.)
Seddon: Seddon, you have muddy pants again. Please go and change them. What were you doing in the mud again, boy?
Sergio: Never shy and often the loudest person present, Sergio expects a lot from people and from life, although he never seems that serious when it gets down to the balls of it.
Setanta: Setanta is what Santa Claus turns into after drinking a bottle and a half of Irish Whisky.  (It’s the only time you’ll see him agro or horny.)
Seth: Just as you begin to say his name it suddenly ends in a twisted mess, which is a similar sensation to suddenly finding yourself in a car that’s about to crash into a wall at speed, when only a few seconds earlier you could have sworn you were lying on the couch and about to fall asleep. Very disconcerting. Depending on the car, the wall and the type of beach, it can be an experience which is either disastrous or bloody funny.
Seymour: Seymour would make a good private detective. He’s fanatical about detail and is obsessed with some of his theories, which he one day hopes to prove.
Shabeer: Muslim. Shabeer’s method of jumping from a diving board is to bounce twice, leaping straight up into the air, bringing the knees up to the chest which are clutched with both hands, and then entering the water with the cheeks full of air and a very serious expression on the face. If done correctly the result is a tremendous explosion.
Shadow: For such a ridiculous name Shadow has turned out quite well. He can joke with anyone - yes, of course he knows he has a strange name - and far from shy away from it, he enjoys the varied reactions that he receives from it. On occasion it's even permitted him to make friends and meet women, so it's not all bad. He won't ever have a regular job, whatever that means.
Shae: The sporting umpire. Wears tight shorts.
Shafiq: Tactful. It would take an outrageous piece of behaviour for Shafiq to stand up and admonish someone at a dinner, for instance. Unless you questioned his parentage, naturally, in which case he’d lunge across the table with whatever implement he could get his hands on. Anything less than that, he’d probably just conspire to catch up with the offending person afterwards.
Shagger: Great mates with Baz, Nugget, Shane and Johnno, Shagger’s role in life is one bordering on the Court Jester, although he’s generally too busy organising the upcoming booze up. Truth be known, he laughs more than he shags, indeed, he even laughs while he’s shaggin’. His girlfriend has a big infectious laugh, just like him.
Shai: Please, tell me lord, that young Shai is an outdoors kind of guy? Coz if he isn't, he'll tear the house apart like a bloody psychotic Jack Russell left alone for a day and half. This boy needs something to do, and he loves the sun. So, ban all video games, banish the TV to the scrap heap, kick him up the arse when he whinges and get him outside.
Shakey: Okay, so his hands tremble, but his mind doesn’t. Almost devoid of an ego, Shakey goes about his business and is quick to lend a hand. He understands motors and wood, and not that I mean to harp on about it but, if anything, his ego could do with a boost.
Shamus: Shamus refuses to pay less than $130 for a bottle of wine.
Shannon: Shannon wanders around in a daze of having little idea what to do. Unlike his female counterpart, his name trails off into nothing and leaves you kind of scratching your head. Although when he does figure it out he can be surprisingly (if not, secretly) industrious.
Sharkey: The funny ratbag who, in heaven, would piss himself with laughter if his death was ever recorded in the Darwin Awards.
Sharne: It took a while for Sharne to figure out his place in life. He’s not Shane and he’s not Shaun, and as a result he works inside using his head and not outside with his hands. That’s not to say one is better than the other, for hard physical work is good for the soul, it’s just a case of Sharne having found his niche. He’s no macho idiot.
Shaun: Shaun deals well in those things that he perceives to be the bare essentials, and this is one of his gifts. He listens to his inner-voice which is usually steady and correct and so, depending on how he is living and where he is in the world, if he deems that he needs to smuggle a cup of hash oil back into the country because he can’t bring himself to throw it out, he will use his impressive intellect and take the proper measures to ensure that (a) he doesn’t get caught and (b) all of his good friends get a chance to enjoy it.
Shaune: Yep, not the most intriguing name but not to worry. Give him a job with his hands and not his acumen, and he’s fine, though, truth be known, he does possess a hidden artistic streak.
Shauny: The last any one heard of him was two weeks ago when he left the resort he was staying at in Morocco, apparently without telling anyone. No one knows what he did with the hash oil that was given to him.
Shawn: " …..Folks are dumb, where I come from…"
Shay: Shay is an obliging man with a humble heart and a physically fit frame. Rarely obese, Shay likes his beans and his nuts and his vegies and his lean meats, and he struggles with the indoor working life. IQ in the mid-range and he has a temper that rises to the quick surprisingly rapidly if pressed.
Sheep: Yep, curly blonde hair on a man who was raised a long way out in the country. Solid and dependable, Sheep is in it for the long haul and yes, as a young man he got to handle plenty of creatures whose name he bears. He ain’t no city slicker.
Shehan: Shehan has a heritage that stems from somewhere near India, possibly Sri Lanka. His name nearly sounds like he’s shearin’, which makes sense because he’s a straight up fellow who is as honest as he is affable.
Sheldon: Sheldon gives an elequant speech but he is awkward on the dance floor and unimaginative in the boudoir.
Shelton: Good friends with Nathan, Shelton has more rules around eating than nearly anyone. The salt and pepper have to placed just so, his drink can't be too full or too empty, the meal has to be at the right temperature and whatever you do, don't speak to him while he's chewing.
Sherman:
First cousin of Herman.
Very high IQ.
Zero common sense.
The school principal wanted to expel him for accidentally setting Miss Johnson’s car on fire, for instance, but how can you expel the smartest kid in the school?
ShimmyTimmy: He might be gay, he might be straight, but whatever he is, he's definitely splendid and he aint no head-kicker. Shimmy Timmy is, however, The Man Most Mysterious. Beyond that, it's anyone's guess...
Shirl: A slightly more polite version of Jimmy.
Shivers: Shivers is more of a beer man, and he tends to keeps most things under wraps.
Shmucka: The actor’s actor who performs even when he’s asleep. It’s a rare gift.
Shoes: Amazing isn't it, that a man can earn a quarter of a million dollars a year and not possess any.
Sholto: A bolt from the blue who seems to trip over his feet occasionally. It’s all that navel gazing that does it, but usually he moves quite freely. A small message, Sholto: what’s the rush, boy?
Shorty: Shorty is a funny guy who is smarter than he looks and who doesn’t ever quit.
Shrek: Sure, his parents are fucking idiots, but that's another story. However, if you think the intellect of the man is wanting you better think again. Yep, Shrek will have his share of detractors and cop his fair share of crap for his name, but hear this: Shrek is like a fledgling company about to list on the stock exchange, and which has a bold, revolutionary new product that will improve life on earth. So, ignore the hype, look into his eyes and invest quick. He doesn't need your assurance, trust me.
Si:
(Pronounced 'sigh'). A nickname of many-a-simons, and a more loving and relaxed version by a long way. The hard-arsed competitive/secretive edge is gone and is replaced with your genial, loving and attentive fellow who everyone knows and adores. And rightly so.

The End.
Sid: Never nasty and dull, Sid gets on well with nearly everyone he meets because he gives them the benefit of the doubt.
Sidney: In a habit that he developed in childhood, whenever he’s awaiting the arrival of his supper, Sidney grasps his knife and fork in each hand and bangs them repetitively and simultaneously on the table, shouting, “Yum, yum! Hungry! Yum yum! Hungry!”
Siegfried: Listen, Siegfried, we've been chatting up here in the commentary box and we suggest you take yourself off to a dramatic acting class. If you're going to carry on like a cheap watch 24/7 you might as well get paid for it. Plus, we'll get some sleep and the umpires can get their breath back.
Siimon: The sort of man that changes his name.
Silas: As a naturally occurring physiological function, and as we’ve mentioned before, Germans don't really understand fart jokes. No, Silas generally isn't a German, but his take on life means that hidden or purely pointless jokes are often lost on him. Great friends with Nicholas, Benjamin and Christian, Silas has a gigantic IQ, detests fools and is quite open about his psychotic tendencies. (Advice from management: if you have one get him away from the city and into the outdoors.)
Silkie:
Silkie has a great desire to reform the education system. (Just kidding!) Indeed, did he go to school? Oh that's right, he started playing in that band and they got a record deal when he was in about year 10. Where is he now? Anyone? 
Oh, really? He's into climbing mountains? Without a safety rope, you say? Oh my god.
Oh well, just don’t tell the insurance companies, eh?
Silvester: Yes, he’s a human. By definition Silvester is a funny guy with no chance of filling a highly responsible/senior position in the company, which, to be honest, is a pity because he’d do a fine job. He’s honest, despite the piss-taking, and he rewards initiative and a keen acumen. He’s also a kinky fucker in the bedroom.
Silvio: Silvio is another grown-up boy whose enthusiasm is occasionally employed to hold up buildings. He has the capacity to be the world’s most adoring friend, as well as your most lethal enemy.
Simeon: Simeon niggles and nestles his way into the ‘cool’ little nooks and crannies of the artistic world.
Simon: Everyone is a scavenger of some sort but this guy is better than most. On any given day Simon is any one of the following: Savvy, Sleazy, Sensible, Sensitive, Selfish and Strong. What makes life interesting for those who him is that he’s one of the few men who can do more than one task at a time, and do them well. Simon can be a smart, slippery customer so we urge you to bear this in mind. So, which Simon have you got today?…
Sinjin: Sinjin encourages the world to come to him, not the other way round.
Skaife: Skaife is quick to point the finger, unless he’s the one trying to pull a swifty.
Skinny: Like Stretch after him, his physique is assumed except that he is oh-so sensitive. Skinny is on life number 2 and he knows it but, like Rhonda way before him, he’s searching desperately for the answers (which probably means that he’s actually on life number 5).
Skip: A nice guy and perhaps a little too nice. Skip is pretty gullable and, like Cecily way before him, he gives more than he recieves. Give him a job where he's occupied and he'll be happy for hours.
Skye: Like his female namesake, the universe presents him with a giant blank canvas. No violent streaks here folks. Skye is a lovely, gentle man.
Slater: Hmmm....is he slippery like Simon? Is he shifty like Solomon? We don't think so, he's not that bright. But, he does tend to make the most of his opportunities, which is fine, so long as his actions and words arise from a position of compassion and forgiveness. Is that the story Slater?...
Slav:
You can imagine the hive of activity in one of London’s best restaurants knowing Prince Harry is dining this evening. Slav, the head chef, agrees to show Harry around the kitchen afterwards but just as Harry enters the space, Slav is caught off guard by an ill-placed tomato broth and an unseen puddle of water on the floor. Harry walks though the doors just as Slav slips over in the kitchen for the first time in 15 years, and hits the deck in unison with 5 litres of puree which spills all over him. 
“So, how was dinner, Harry?” Slav asks, looking up and wiping the broth out of his eyes.
Harry smiles. “Splendid Slav, just splendid. I just wanted to say how much I enjoyed dinner. Lucky I didn’t order the tomato soup, eh?”
“Yes, well, I can tell you that it tastes great.”
“Mmmm, it looks it.”


This is classic Slav.
Slimey: True to the cause. He can pick a faker a long way off.
Smiddy: If Smiddy is a room full of people then there is only one of them on Earth. I have no idea what would happen to the universe if ever there were two. It might just implode for something funny and cool to do. Who knows....
Smiley:
Whether he’s about to speak with the Prime Minister or he’s in the middle of getting 4 crazy kids off to school, it’s difficult for Smiley to get loaded up with the stresses of responsibility. His name catches the world off-guard, which keeps him light on his feet, partially because he is continually on the look-out for anything new; be it weird coincidences, new toys, unusual recipes or undiscovered coral species. 
(Closet sexual deviant.)
Smith:
Ooookay, so either mum was besotted with the waiter-character from the TV show, Sex In The City, or….hang on…in fact….there is no ‘either’. 
Smith’s mother was infatuated with the Smith waiter-character from the TV show Sex In The City, and there it is. But what does this mean? Oddly enough, Smith does alright. He’s understated, although, yes, his ego isn’t minimal, but he’s in for good people and good times, and he’ll assist strangers if he remembers that he can. He’s not a total dill, by a long shot.
Smithy: You say his name, and it sweeps over the ground barely touching it. What does that mean, you ask? Well, it means that he's rarely in one spot for very long, he picks up friends easily - sometimes too easily, so his girlfriends will tell you! - he lives in the moment and he doesn't really like clutter. Smithy.
Snap: Pass. Is he a drug dealer?..Anyone?
Snapper: His friends are all men aside from his girlfriend, who tolerates his excessive drinking. Usually she’s partaking and in that regard they’re a good couple. Snapper spends a lot of time talking about engines and possibly boats. Never done so much as a sit-up in his life.
Sol:
You’ve entered the lift and next stop, Bang, the head of the company steps in. And you’ve always had an idea, haven’t you? You now have 30 seconds to pitch it to them from a random, standing start, and if it’s good they’ll listen:
Sol lives for these moments. It’s why he’s successful, this coolness under pressure. It makes him think faster and more clearly.
Soon enough,  usually, Sol becomes the boss stepping into the lift, and so life goes around again.
Solaris: Oh for Christ's sake.....Solaris? (Sigh).......Okay, well let's just ignore mum and dad, who were hoping to produce a unique soul predestined to make a singular, magnificent contribution to human kind. Mmmmm, well, we can tell you Solaris is nice fellow, with a genial approach to life, and a room full of incense sticks, Tibetan prayer flags and books about the Dalai Llama. When he gets back from yoga and brushes the hair out of his face we'll catch up with him and see what he's up to...
Solomon: The card shark. He speaks in low tones in lieu of all those O’s, which rumble in the back of your throat like the ominous rumblings of an over-regulating government. He understands the tax system backwards.
Sonny: The Walking Ego, and that's okay. He has a smile on his face and a million friends, most of whom only know him as that big happy guy.
Sooty: He's a cheeky little bugger, isn't he?
Soren: A self-conscious fellow who would do better than he is if he didn't care so much about what others think. Soren, here's a tip, on their death bed everyone is only thinking about what is about to happen next. What you do and how you do it won't get a look in. (We'll talk about your kids another day.)
Soul: Your local, friendly drug dealer. Nice guy. But he’s a drug dealer, in case that bothers you.
Soz: The remarkable cat with nine lives. (Note: He's got about 2 left....maybe even 1.)
Spearo: Smooth in water. Ungainly on land.
Spencer: Spencer loves golf clothes despite his inability to play the game. (He has a fetish for fishnet stockings and he secretly wears them under his trousers during competition.)
Spike: Like his namesake on a mathematical graph, Spike is capable of either the best or the worst and, thankfully, there isn’t too much middle ground.
Spiro: A man of his word. Yes, he has a sense of humour, but the rigours of a respected male life run deep and are not easily shrugged off. Spiro is therefore rarely flippant and family is very important to him.
Splinter: Splinter is awkward, hardworking and brave.
Spock: Like his namesake from the Starship Enterprise, he was born with gifts that are often misunderstood by those in the human world. The question is, how will he discover them, and what will he do once he does?
Stacy: Stacy never sits still for long. He's a quick thinker and a logical one, and he moves over the ground rapidly and with a destination in mind. His family are an odd but lovely bunch and we, up here in the commentary box, believe that most people could actually learn a lot by watching how Stacy performs.
Stamos: Perpetually surprised and aghast at how poorly his magnificent plan worked out, Stamos refuses to give up. Why would you?
Stamps: The tall, gentle and unflustered man (on the surface, at least). He’d make an excellent fireman.
Stan: Mates with Jim and Bruce, Stan was never the most excitable bloke. He grumbles about the weather.
Stanley: Stanley tucks his shirt in without fail, he ensures his shoes are nicely polished and when his arthritis allows it, and whenever he’s in such a position, which is a rarity these days, he opens car doors for ladies.
Stas: Of Russian extraction, Stas will hold his own, have a laugh with you, but expect that you are able to hold your own, also.
Stavros: See that horse out there in the equestrian arena prancing around like a bloody trumped-up poodle, with all that ridiculous head-dress regal rubbish all over his face? If Stavros could watch himself fart, he would.
StClair: Some of the things St.Clair does to himself in the name of self-pleasuring would make even the most worldly Jake wince. Indeed, they're too graphic even for these pages. So, all we say is, St.Clair, be careful, wash your hands and it's  your turn to cook.
Stede: Stede is a city boy and to that end his take on horses is thus: If you can’t put petrol in it don’t get on it. Aside from these urban attitudes, Stede tends to surround himself with the male of the species, which is fine, I suppose. It’s a little boring if you ask us but no one is perfect.
Steele: Steele walks around all concerned, as if his nuts are about to drop off. Relax, brother……just relax.
Steen:
He's not so much a stain on society, as he is a stain on the walls and buildings upon which he applies his not insignificant artistic prowess. 
And we're not talking about just some stock-standard, desperate-looking tag, aching to be recognised. Steen, the boy, and possibly always the boy, has talent, so let's see how he goes...
Stefan:
Stefan rhymes with, “Spitting an olive pip out of your mouth that’s just cut your cheek and nearly cracked a tooth as you bit into it by mistake.” 
(Note: Remembering, of course, that olives are tasty and nutritious, and that Stefan’s substantial physical and/or intellectual capabilities may one day save your life.)
Stefano: God love him. Yep, his restaurant is going down the drain and he's in debt up to his eyeballs, but you'd never know. The smile and the embrace he gives you as you enter are real, and while behind the curtain things are dire, hospitality is his game and his life. Chin up, Stefano. Things always come good again…
Steinley: Like a classical pianist, Steinley has clean hands and lean, agile fingers. The neurons in his grey matter are connected up so well and with such intensity that they convey information and imaginings faster than Einstein in his heyday. And best of all, ladies and gentlemen, his eyes sparkle like the Good Witch’s magic crystal ball.......fret not young friar, they cried, for the King is imminent!
Stephan: Large IQ, low level of patience for fuckwits, high technical ability, no idea how to change the oil in his car, prefers cats to dogs, good under pressure and many people find his sense of humour so dry and pragmatic that they just don't get him.
Stephen:
Neat, fussy and often lean or small in stature, Stephen won’t wear underpants unless they are properly ironed. By preparing well at every level of his waking life he enables his financial services business to thrive like few others, and he is now quite wealthy as a result. 
(Note: Stephen is completely unrelated to Steve, and he feels very uncomfortable whenever anyone refers to him by that name.)
Steve: Steve walks a fine line. V is a powerful letter that can provide immediate greatness, depending on where it is, but if too much time is spent on the ‘ee’ before you get to the V, Steve may well turn out to be a truly sly prick. If it is kept short, however, he can be one of the great individuals. Funny as well. See how you go….
Steven: Steven thinks that only immoral women give head.
Stevie: Stevie is greasy, slimy and sleazy like a low-grade hustler in Mexico City.
Stevo: Like Walshy and Johnno, everyone knows Stevo’.
Stewart: An English-styled buffoon who is very polite on the surface.
Stirling: A private school ponce who is the first to volunteer to go into battle for King and country, primarily so he can bed the women who are attracted to his uniform that sports lots of little gold tassels and shiny metal bits from when he once blew up a tribe of African natives using cannons. (He avoids walking near primary schools because all the children point at him and yell, “G’day Peacock!”)
Stoane: No, he doesn't smile all the time but trust me, it’s a front. Deep down Stoane is a big fuzzy bear just doing his thing, and yes, he can’t move without breaking something but it’s never deliberate. Don’t be frightened.
Stone:
Does Stone keep his opinions to himself? 
Yes.
Is Stone irresponsible? 
No, he most definitely isn’t, although he’s not always strictly legal. 
Would he forgo the opportunity of stealing a late model BMW convertible sitting unattended by the beach with the keys in the ignition, if he saw a child being swept out to sea? 
Of course he would. Funny thing is, after receiving his bravery award from the mayor at the council chambers, months later, afterwards all he’d have to do is wait around for an hour before he meets with his parole board, which is taking place in the same building.
And don’t you worry, Stone fully appreciates the irony of such situations, which is why we like him.
Stoner: Stoner is upbeat, energetic and adventurous.
Storm: Bloody lost in a storm more like it. Or is that is parents? Anyway, rather than become a tempest, Storm shies away from the spotlight and lets just pray he manages to steer away from the dodgy part of town…
Stretch: Stretch is a good, humorous and reliable individual who kind of lopes along the street in the same way that he lopes along through life. Like his female namesake, Stretch is invariably tall.
Struan:
It's the middle of the night and the storm descended on the ketch in a flash. The spinnaker is torn to shreds before anyone can react and suddenly the vessel is in peril. Struan, the first mate, has seen it all before and over the howling noise of the gale he shouts, “Just cut it free. Quickly now.”
The panic-stricken owner begins to protest at a $40,000 sail about to be discarded forever and Struan looks at him calmly. 
“Listen, do you want to live or do you want to die?...”
Stu: Soft like a sponge, Stu can deal with any situation. He’s probably the most adaptable and malleable of all the male species and a better absorber of shock or strangeness does not exist. One day he’ll be canonised and we will then know him as St. Stu. And rightly so.
Stuart: An upstanding member of society who helps out in community projects, such as Meals On Wheels. His mother insists that he eat Sunday lunch at her house every weekend, much to his initial chagrin, although when the apple pie comes out he wouldn’t be anywhere else. And he loves his mum.
Stubbsy: Stubbsy collects his beer and his bowl of hot chips from the bar, dodges and weaves back to his friends' table and when he arrives he plonks the beer down, stuffing a couple of chips into his mouth as he sits. Immediately, a horrified look appears on his face. Shocking his friends and all those nearby, Stubbsy pushes his seat back in disgust, stands up again, puts an open palm next to his mouth and yells across a crowded pub, "HEY MATE! YOU FORGOT THE FUCKIN' SALT!"  Stubbsy.
Stuey: Stuey is a lovely bloke who will do anything for anyone, if need be, (which is a product of the softness of his name) and as a trade-off he often lacks a potent killer-instinct.
Suede: Yes, Suede was conceived on the old couch and his parents, bless, wanted to be different. Anyway, Suede is a highly principled lad who will dabble with the arts. Which one, exactly, is uncertain but he definitely won't be doing anything with leather.
Suede-Butterfly: What is it with some of you hippies? I'm all for free love in all directions, but honestly! Why didn't you call him Wood-Anchovy? Or Aluminium-Nematode? (Sigh) Anyway, Suede-Butterfly has had earrings since he was 2 months old – like he had a say in the matter – and he’ll go to his grave having not once donned a suit and not once proclaiming to have been in a position of responsibility. So, it’s not all bad.
Sully: Deepest darkest Africa. 1930's. Sully blazes into the tent wearing tweed jodpurs and an open white linen shirt, half unbuttoned, covered in sweat and with a rifle slung over his shoulder. He usually exudes charisma and charm, but not today. "There's a flood," he says calmly. "We need to leave. Now." So, with style and not a moment to spare everyone is saved. Sully.
Sundeep: Is Sundeep the most gullible man in the Kingdom? Perhaps. But this generosity of expectation also makes him happy and reasonably loveable. He wants a big family and would probably prefer sons to daughters. (Sundeep, if this is your desire can we suggest that this is unmitigated bullshit and you’ve been brainwashed by your peers and family. Do you think women aren’t at least as powerful as men? They’re definitely more peace-loving.)
Sunny: Forget corporate achievement or material gain, for Sunny is powered by a different kind of sun – a connected, hilarious and spiritual one.
Sven: Like a short lick of a potent and over-ripe cheese, Sven has a unique and complex flavour. He’s a highly intelligent and optimistic fellow and if you’re chasing an intense journey in the name of love or friendship, he could be your man.
Swain: Rarely does Swain trod the straight and narrow path. There are always shortcuts, you see. At least in his mind, anyway. There's always an easier route, a smoother passage, a more profitable way of doing things. Swain therefore tends to focus on the desintation not the journey. He'd make a useless Buddhist.
Swampy: As an outgoing and loudish-mouthed egotist, Swampy is ideal to have around when a group conversation has become uncomfortably stilted. In this setting his presence will be secretly adored by all those present.
Sylvester:
"Ah, well, if it isn't the culprit from last night who stole the car, spilt crap all over the carpet and set fire to the neighbours tree. What are you doing showing your face back here?"
Sylvester kicks the ground in front of him. “Well, I won 30 grand at the casino after I left last night. So I thought I’d come back and mend some bridges.”
Sylvester, mate, we appreciate it, but how about next time we keep the bridges in tact in the first place. Management.
Sylvian: Sylvian is that guy in the movies who is one hurdle away from getting to the treasure. He's crossed the planet, risking life and limb, and you can see in his eyes that he knew he'd get this far. On the other hand, of course, his job is not over and the toughest test is about to begin. Question is, will Sylvian prevail? His French heritage means he loves the constant melodrama, but that’s another story.
Symmo: Symmo is a blend of Walshy, Johnno, Marty, Dave and Pedro.
Symon: Symon has never held a hammer and gets a manicure every fortnight.
Sĕan:
No one can tell you about Sean and so you will have to go and find out for yourself. You’ll need to walk up into the hills and seek out that old guy with the dogs. He’ll give you some bizarre instructions and a special leather pouch that, hopefully, will contain a strange amulet. Sounds weird, huh? Anyway, many people have vanished trying to find him but what I can tell you is that he is a good and remarkable man – if he is a man. 
(Note: There are rumours that he has human bones hanging from his ears and is over 13,000 years old.....)
